content.title: The Mystery of the Cool Matka
content.text: Have you ever wondered why water kept in an earthen pot (matka) during summer stays incredibly cool, even when it's boiling hot outside? Or why you shiver when you step out of a swimming pool on a windy day?

ai_context.tutor_hint: Ask the student what happens to the water on their skin when they stand under a fan.

content.title: Think Like a Scientist
content.prompt: If heat is needed to turn liquid water into vapor, where does the water on your skin (or the outside of a matka) get that heat from before it disappears? Take a guess!

content.title: Evaporation Cooling Effect
content.caption: A sweating traditional Indian mud pot (matka) cooling the water inside through evaporation.

content.title: Evaporation (Bāṣpībhavana)
content.text: Evaporation is the phenomenon of change of a liquid into vapors at any temperature below its boiling point. Etymology: From Latin 'evaporare' (to disperse in vapor). In Sanskrit, it relates to 'Bāṣpa' (Vapor/Tears) and 'Bhavana' (Becoming).
content.key_insight: The particles at the surface gain enough energy from the surroundings to overcome the forces of attraction and change into vapor, taking away heat and leaving the surface cooler.

content.question: Which of the following factors increases the rate of evaporation?
content.explanation: Increasing wind speed blows away the water vapor particles, allowing more liquid to evaporate faster.

content.title: Your Turn to Reflect
content.prompt: Explain to your younger sibling why we prefer wearing cotton clothes in summer using the concept of evaporation.

content.title: Connecting to Geography
content.text: Evaporation is a crucial step in the Water Cycle (Hydrologic Cycle). Without evaporation from oceans and rivers, there would be no cloud formation and no rain!

content.title: Mastery Challenge
content.text: If you spill a drop of water and a drop of alcohol on your palm, which one will feel colder, and why? Conduct this thought experiment!
